**HR & Payroll Management System**

Product Requirements Document (PRD)

# **1\. Document Overview**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Product Name | HR & Payroll Management System |
| Product Type | Web-based HR and payroll platform |
| Frontend | React (or equivalent modern framework), Tailwind CSS |
| Backend | REST API server with business logic and payroll calculation engine |
| Database | MySQL relational database (30+ tables) |
| Version | 1.3 — Draft, pending stakeholder review |
| Date | September 10, 2026 |

# **2\. Product Vision**

Give the company a centralized, web-based system for managing its complete HR and payroll cycle — employee records, attendance, leave, loans, bonuses, deductions, and monthly salary generation — replacing manual spreadsheets and disconnected tools with one accurate, auditable, and self-service platform that keeps every payroll run compliant with current NBR income tax rules.

# **3\. Product Goals**

•     Allow employees to apply for leave, request loans and advances, and view their own attendance and payslips without going through HR manually.

•     Allow managers to review and approve leave, loan, overtime, and attendance-correction requests from their team.

•     Allow HR to onboard, configure, and manage employees, salary structures, leave policy, bonuses, and increments from one place.

•     Allow Finance to run a monthly payroll cycle that automatically pulls attendance, allowances, bonuses, deductions, and loan EMIs into an accurate net salary.

•     Calculate income tax automatically according to the NBR slab in force, without hard-coding the rate.

•     Capture attendance automatically from a biometric device instead of manual entry.

•     Control what each role can see and do through configurable permissions, and keep a complete audit trail of all system actions.

•     Provide exportable reports on headcount, attendance, leave, payroll cost, and tax for review and audit.

# **4\. Target Users & Roles**

| Role | Primary needs |
| :---- | :---- |
| Admin | Manage system configuration, security settings, roles and permissions, company profile, departments, and designations — full access across the system. |
| HR | Manage the complete employee lifecycle, leave, loan, bonus, increment, and initiate payroll runs. |
| Manager / Approver | Approve leave, loan, overtime, and attendance-correction requests from direct reports. |
| Finance / Accounts | Review and finalize monthly payroll runs and ensure income tax deductions comply with the current NBR slab. |
| Employee | Apply for leave and loans, view personal attendance records, and download monthly payslips. |

*Role-based access is intentionally expandable: roles and permissions are first-class entities, so new roles or finer-grained permissions can be introduced without a structural change.*

# **5\. Functional Requirements**

Each module below describes its purpose, lists its requirements, and states the acceptance criteria used to confirm correct behaviour. Full requirement identifiers (e.g. ATT-01, SAL-03) are in the companion SRS document.

## **5.1 Dashboard  —  Should have**

***Description***

The dashboard gives every user a role-appropriate, at-a-glance view of the system the moment they log in, so they never have to open individual modules just to check current status.

***Requirements***

•     Display a role-based dashboard immediately after login, with a different view for Admin/HR and for Employee.

•     Show summary widgets for total employees, employees present today, employees on leave, and pending approvals.

•     Show a payroll status widget for the current cycle (draft, approved, or locked).

•     Chart the week's attendance trend and the department-wise employee distribution.

•     Give employees a personal summary: attendance, leave balance, and a quick shortcut to apply for leave.

•     List upcoming holidays, birthdays, and work anniversaries.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     Logging in as Admin/HR shows organisation-wide widgets; logging in as an Employee shows a personal summary instead.

•     The payroll status widget reflects the actual current-cycle status.

•     Charts update when the underlying attendance or headcount data changes.

Fig:Dashboard Module  
 

## **5.2 Security  —  Must have**

***Description***

The security module protects the system by controlling who can log in, what they can do, and keeping a traceable record of every sensitive action.

***Requirements***

•     Support role-based access control with configurable roles: Admin, HR, Manager, Employee, Accounts.

•     Allow an authorized Admin to create, edit, and deactivate user accounts.

•     Enforce a minimum password policy and support password reset via email or one-time password.

•     Log every create, update, delete, and approve action with the user, timestamp, and IP address.

•     Automatically end an idle session after a configurable timeout.

•     Restrict each module's view/add/edit/delete/approve actions according to the logged-in user's role.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     A deactivated account cannot log in.

•     Changing a role's permissions takes effect for its users the next time permissions are read.

•     Every create/update/delete/approve action appears in the audit log with the correct user and timestamp.

•     An idle session is logged out automatically after the configured period.

![][image2]

Fig:Security Module

 

## **5.3 Setting  —  Should have**

***Description***

The setting module lets Admin configure company-wide data once, so every other module runs on consistent, centrally managed values.

***Requirements***

•     Configure the company profile: name, logo, address, and registration number.

•     Configure departments and designations within each department.

•     Configure the payroll cycle as monthly, with a fixed salary-generation date.

•     Configure the annual holiday calendar and standard working days and hours.

•     Configure notification and email settings for approvals and payslip delivery.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     Company profile and department/designation changes are reflected wherever they are used, such as employee onboarding.

•     The payroll cycle date configured here drives when the monthly payroll run becomes available.

## **5.4 Employee Configuration  —  Should have**

***Description***

This module defines reusable grade and salary templates so HR does not rebuild the same setup for every new hire.

***Requirements***

•     Define employee grades and categories with an associated salary range.

•     Define a salary structure template per grade, comprising Basic percentage, HRA percentage, and other allowance percentages.

•     Configure required employee document types as mandatory or optional.

•     Support an auto-generation rule for a unique employee identifier on onboarding.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     Assigning a grade to a new employee automatically applies the correct salary structure template.

•     Onboarding cannot be completed without the required document types.

 **5.5 Loan & Advance Management  —  Should have**

***Description***

This module handles employee loan and advance requests and recovers them automatically through monthly payroll.

***Requirements***

•     Configure loan and advance types with interest rate if applicable, maximum amount, and maximum tenure.

•     Allow an employee to apply for a loan or advance with an auto-calculated EMI preview before submission.

•     Route the request to HR or Finance for approval or rejection.

•     Generate an EMI repayment schedule automatically on approval.

•     Deduct the monthly EMI from salary automatically during payroll generation until fully repaid.

•     Maintain a loan ledger showing outstanding balance and repayment history per employee.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     The EMI shown to the employee before submission matches the EMI actually deducted later.

•     A loan stops appearing as a deduction once it is fully repaid.

## **5.6 Bonus Management  —  Should have**

***Description***

This module lets HR generate festival or performance bonuses for many employees at once, with room to adjust individual amounts before finalizing.

***Requirements***

•     Configure bonus types with a calculation rule of either a fixed amount or a percentage of basic salary.

•     Generate bonuses in bulk for all eligible employees or a filtered subset by department or grade.

•     Allow manual adjustment of an individual employee's bonus amount before finalization.

•     Include the finalized bonus amount automatically in the corresponding payroll run.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     A bulk-generated bonus batch can be adjusted for one employee without affecting the rest.

•     A finalized bonus appears correctly on the employee's payslip for that cycle.

## **5.7 Allowance Module  —  Should have**

***Description***

This module configures the recurring allowance components that form part of an employee's gross salary.

***Requirements***

•     Configure allowance types such as Transport, Medical, House Rent, and Food with a taxable or non-taxable flag and gross salary calculation.

•     Assign allowances to employees individually or in bulk by grade.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     Assigning an allowance by grade applies it to every employee in that grade going forward.

## **5.8 Increment Module  —  Could have**

***Description***

This module processes salary increments through an approval step and keeps a full history for later reference.

***Requirements***

•     Configure an increment policy expressed as a percentage or a fixed amount with eligibility criteria.

•     Process an increment for an individual employee or in bulk by department.

•     Require approval before an increment is applied to an active salary structure.

•     Retain a complete increment history including prior salary, revised salary, and effective date per employee.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     An increment takes effect on salary generation only after it has been approved.

•     The increment history for an employee shows every past change, not only the most recent one.

 

## **5.9 Deduction Module  —  Must have**

***Description***

This module calculates all salary deductions, including income tax, based on the NBR slab currently in force.

***Requirements***

•     Configure deduction types, both statutory and non-statutory, with an associated calculation rule.

•     Configure the NBR income tax slab table with income range and tax percentage, editable by Admin whenever NBR revises the rate.

•     Automatically calculate monthly income tax withholding from projected annual taxable income and the configured slab.

•     Automatically apply configured deductions such as absence penalty and provident fund during payroll generation.

•     Produce a deduction breakdown per employee per cycle for audit and payslip purposes.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     Updating the tax slab table changes future payroll tax calculations without any code change.

•     The tax amount shown on a payslip matches what the configured slab produces for that employee's income.

 

## **5.10 Leave Management — Must have**

### ***Description***

This module lets employees apply for leave against a real-time balance and routes each request through a configurable multi-level approval workflow, keeping balances and attendance consistent across the system.

### ***Requirements***

* Configure leave types (Casual, Sick, Earned, Unpaid, Maternity) with a paid/unpaid flag and an annual maximum entitlement, per employee grade where applicable.

* Allocate a leave balance per employee, per leave type, per year based on the assigned policy.  
* Allow an employee to submit a leave request specifying leave type, date range, and reason.  
* Auto-calculate the number of days requested, accounting for weekends and holidays as configured, and validate against the employee's remaining balance.  
* Route the request through a multi-level approval workflow: reporting manager first, then HR final approval — the request status reflects the current stage (Pending Manager Review → Pending HR Review → Approved/Rejected).  
* Block a request that exceeds the available balance unless HR explicitly overrides it.  
* Deduct approved leave days from the balance automatically only upon final (HR) approval — never at the manager-approval stage.  
* On final approval, automatically mark the corresponding date range as On-Leave in Attendance.  
* On rejection at either stage, mark the request Rejected with an optional reason; no balance is deducted.  
* Support configurable year-end carry-forward rules per leave type.  
* Display a leave calendar showing all employees currently on approved leave, for team/company-wide planning.

### ***Acceptance Criteria***

* An employee cannot submit a request for more days than their remaining balance without an explicit HR override.  
* Approving at manager level moves the request to HR review, not directly to Approved status.  
* The leave balance decreases only after final (HR) approval, never before.  
* A final-approved leave request appears as On-Leave in Attendance for the exact date range, with no manual entry required.  
* A rejected request at either stage leaves the employee's balance unchanged.  
* The leave calendar accurately reflects all currently approved leave for the selected period.

## **5.11 Attendance Management — Must have**

### ***Description***

This module captures daily attendance automatically from the biometric device, with a manual correction path for exceptions, and provides the attendance data that Overtime and Salary Generation depend on.

### ***Requirements***

* Import daily check-in and check-out records from the biometric device via file import, device API, or SDK integration.  
* Match imported records to the correct employee using the employee's biometric or device identifier.  
* Automatically classify each day as Present, Late, Half-Day, or Absent based on configured shift start/end times and grace period rules.  
* Allow HR/Admin to manually add or correct an attendance record when biometric data is missing or incorrect, with every manual change logged (editor, timestamp, previous value, reason).  
* Allow an employee to submit an attendance regularization request with a reason, subject to manager approval, for cases where the biometric record is wrong or missing.  
* Automatically mark attendance as On-Leave for approved leave dates, overriding any biometric absence for that date.  
* Automatically mark company holidays (from the Setting Module's holiday calendar) as Holiday for all employees, without requiring a device record.  
* Provide a monthly attendance summary per employee (present/absent/late/half-day/on-leave/holiday counts) for use by Overtime and Salary Generation.

### ***Acceptance Criteria***

* A day with approved leave never shows as Absent, even if the biometric device recorded nothing.  
* A manually corrected or regularized record is distinguishable from an auto-imported record in the audit log.  
* A check-in after the configured grace period is automatically flagged Late.  
* The monthly summary total for an employee matches the sum of their daily status counts for that month.  
* An approved attendance regularization request updates the affected day's status and is reflected in that month's summary.

 **5.12 Overtime Configuration Module — Should have**

### 

### ***Description***

This module calculates overtime pay automatically from attendance data using a configurable rate, with manager approval required for any hours beyond what attendance data supports.

### 

### ***Requirements***

* Configure an overtime rate multiplier (e.g., 1.5x standard hourly rate on weekdays, 2x on holidays) and the maximum permitted overtime hours per day; rules may vary by grade or department.  
* Calculate eligible overtime hours automatically from attendance data (check-out time beyond shift end plus a configurable minimum threshold) or from an employee-submitted manual request (e.g., pre-planned weekend work).  
* Require manager approval for any overtime hours beyond what attendance data directly supports (i.e., all manually submitted requests).  
* Calculate overtime pay as hours × hourly rate × configured multiplier, and include it automatically in the relevant payroll run.  
* Provide HR a per-employee, per-cycle overtime summary for review before Salary Generation runs.

### ***Acceptance Criteria***

* Overtime is only counted when actual worked time exceeds shift end by more than the configured threshold, or via an approved manual request.  
* Overtime pay on a payslip matches hours × rate × multiplier exactly.  
* Overtime beyond what attendance data supports is not paid without manager approval.  
* The per-cycle overtime summary correctly aggregates all approved overtime instances for each employee within that period.

## **5.13 Employee Module  —  Must have**

***Description***

This module is the single source of employee data, covering onboarding through separation.

***Requirements***

•     Support employee onboarding through a multi-step form covering personal information, employment details, bank details, documents, and emergency contact.

•     Allow document upload and storage against configured document types.

•     Provide a searchable and filterable employee directory by department, designation, and status.

•     Provide an employee profile view with sections for attendance, leave, loan, salary history, and documents.

•     Support a separation process for resignation or termination, capturing date, reason, and a clearance checklist.

•     Block a separated employee's login from the recorded separation date onward.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     Onboarding cannot be completed without required fields and documents.

•     A separated employee cannot log in after their separation date, even with correct credentials.

![][image15]

Fig: Employee Module

 **5.14 Salary Generation Module  —  Must have**

***Description***

This module runs the monthly payroll, pulling in attendance, allowances, bonuses, deductions, and loan EMIs to produce an accurate, auditable salary for every employee.

***Requirements***

•     Generate payroll on a monthly cycle for all active employees.

•     Calculate gross salary as Basic plus Allowances plus Bonus plus Overtime.

•     Calculate net salary as Gross minus Deductions minus Loan EMI minus NBR income tax.

•     Present a payroll run in Draft status for HR or Finance review before approval.

•     Allow an authorized user to Approve and then Lock a run; a locked run cannot be edited.

•     Generate an individual PDF payslip per employee, viewable and downloadable by that employee.

•     Retain a salary revision history and prevent an unaudited overwrite of a locked payroll run.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     The net salary shown for each employee matches Gross minus all deductions exactly.

•     A locked payroll run rejects any direct edit; a correction requires a new, audited adjustment entry.

•     Every employee's payslip is available for download once the run is approved.

![][image16]  
 					Fig:Salary Generation Module

 

## **5.15 Reporting  —  Should have**

***Description***

This module gives management and finance exportable, filterable visibility into HR and payroll operations.

***Requirements***

•     Provide an employee headcount report by department and by joining and leaving trend.

•     Provide attendance and leave reports filterable by employee, department, and date range.

•     Provide a monthly and yearly payroll cost report by department.

•     Provide a loan and advance outstanding report and an income tax deduction report.

•     Allow export of any report to PDF and Excel formats.

***Acceptance Criteria***

•     Applying a filter narrows the report correctly without extra steps.

•     An exported PDF or Excel report matches what is shown on screen.

# **6\. Non-Functional Requirements**

## **6.1 Performance**

Monthly payroll generation for up to 500 employees should complete within 2 minutes. Standard list and search pages should load within 2 seconds under normal load.

## **6.2 Security**

Passwords must be stored using a one-way, salted hash and never in plain text. All data in transit must be encrypted over HTTPS/TLS, and every financial or approval action must be captured in the audit log.

## **6.3 Reliability**

A locked payroll run must be immutable; any correction requires an explicit, audited adjustment entry rather than a direct edit. The database should be backed up automatically on a daily basis.

## **6.4 Usability**

Employee self-service pages — leave application, loan application, and payslip view — should work cleanly on a mobile browser without horizontal scrolling.

## **6.5 Maintainability**

Tax slabs, leave policy, and allowance, deduction, and bonus rules should be configurable by Admin or HR directly without requiring a code change.

## **6.6 Scalability**

The system should be designed so additional modules can be added without major changes to existing functionality. The roles and permissions structure already supports this for access control.

 

# **7\. Data Model**

The application is backed by a relational schema (MySQL) of more than 30 tables. Primary and foreign keys enforce referential integrity throughout — for example, a Payslip cannot reference a nonexistent Employee or Payroll Run. Full column-level detail is in the companion database schema document.

| Area | Tables |
| :---- | :---- |
| Organisation & Access | Department, Designation, Grade, Branch, Role, Permission, User, AuditLog |
| Employee | Employee, EmergencyContact, EmployeeDocument |
| Attendance | Attendance, AttendanceCorrection, AttendanceRegularizationRequest, OvertimeRequest, HolidayCalendarr |
| Leave | LeaveType, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest |
| Compensation Setup | SalaryStructureTemplate, AllowanceType, DeductionType, TaxSlab, IncrementPolicy |
| Employee Compensation | EmployeeAllowance, EmployeeDeduction, Increment |
| Loan | LoanType, LoanRequest, LoanRepayment |
| Bonus | BonusType, BonusRun |
| Payroll | PayrollRun, Payslip |
| System Settings | CompanySetting, FinancialYear, NotificationSetting |

# **10\. User Flow**

Below is the high-level user flow for the system, showing how each role navigates from login through their primary tasks to payroll output.

| User | Primary flow |
| :---- | :---- |
| Admin | Login → Security (roles, permissions, users) → Setting (company, departments, holiday calendar) |
| HR | Login → Employee Module (onboard/manage) → Leave / Loan / Bonus / Increment / Overtime→ Salary Generation |
| Manager | Login → Dashboard (pending approvals) → Approve leave / loan / OT / attendance regularization /manual overtime requests |
| Finance | Login → Salary Generation (review draft → approve → lock) → Reporting (tax, payroll cost) |
| Employee | Login → Dashboard → Apply leave / Apply loan → Attendance (view, regularize) → Payslip download |

# **11\. Release Plan**

| Phase | Includes | Objective |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Phase 1 (MVP) | Security, Leave, Deduction/Tax, Attendance (biometric), Employee Module, Salary Generation | A legally compliant, usable monthly payroll cycle |
| Phase 2 | Dashboard, Setting, Employee Configuration, Loan, Bonus, Allowance, Overtime, Reporting | Full operational efficiency and employee self-service |
| Phase 3 | Increment Module and any deferred enhancements | Refinement and supplementary workflow automation |

# **12\. Success Criteria**

The project is considered successful for this phase when users can:

•     Log in and see a dashboard scoped correctly to their role.

•     Apply for leave and loan, and see the request move through the approval chain without manual follow-up.

•     See attendance captured automatically from the biometric device, with a clear path to correct exceptions.

•     Run monthly payroll and receive an accurate net salary, with income tax calculated per the current NBR slab.

•     Download a correct, individual payslip once a payroll run is approved.

•     Export headcount, attendance, leave, payroll cost, and tax reports for review.

•     Rely on the system and its audit trail with no data loss or unexplained calculation differences.
